subject: botany
question_text: What is meant by emasculation? When and why does a plant breeder employ this technique?

page_header: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants · 4 marks

steps.label: Definition

lines.text: Emasculation = removal of the anthers from a
bisexual flower of the female parent

lines: It is done while the flower is still in the
bud condition, before the anthers open.
steps.why: The definition needs the organ removed (anthers), the flower type (bisexual), the plant (the chosen female parent) and the stage (bud) — each word closes a loophole through which selfing could happen.
common_mistakes: Writing 'removal of stamens from any flower' — it is specifically the female parent in a planned cross.
Removing the anthers after the flower opens — by then its own pollen may already be shed.
steps.memory_tip: E-MASculation removes the MALE parts — anthers out, in the bud.
steps.margin_note: Both boxed lines together are the 2-mark definition; the bud timing sits with them.

steps.label: When it is done
lines: It is used during artificial hybridisation in
plant breeding programmes, on the flower bud
of the plant selected as the female parent.
steps.why: The 'when' has two layers: the programme (artificial hybridisation) and the stage (the bud, before anther dehiscence) — both must appear.
common_mistakes: Answering only 'in plant breeding' without the bud stage.
Emasculating the male parent — its pollen is the one being used, not removed.
steps.memory_tip: Before the bud opens, before the pollen escapes — that is the only window.
steps.margin_note: One sentence naming hybridisation and the bud stage covers this mark.

steps.why: The purpose completes the technique: no self pollen means every seed on the female parent is the planned cross, which is how a breeder combines desired characters.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 'to avoid self-pollination' — add what that buys: hybrids with desirable characters.
Mixing up emasculation with bagging. Cutting anthers is emasculation; the cover is bagging.
steps.memory_tip: Cut (emasculate) → cover (bag) → cross (dust chosen pollen). Emasculation is step one of the chain.
steps.margin_note: Give both halves of the why: stop selfing AND produce the desired hybrid.

insider_note: The question asks what, when and why — three explicit asks. Answer them in that order with headings and no mark can be missed for structure.
